newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian-Israeli refinery survives peace stalemate.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian-Israeli refinery survives peace stalemate.

text.p: The Egyptian investor in a joint-venture oil refinery with Israelis said on Thursday the project would go ahead despite the stalemate in peace talks.

"We are businessmen...We have nothing to do with politics," said Hussein Salem, chairman of Middle East Oil Refinery (MIDOR), which is building the 100,000 barrels per day refinery west of the Egyptian city of Alexandria.
He was speaking at a news conference on the sidelines of the Middle East economic conference, where some delegates questioned the possibility of working with Israelis now.

The oil refinery, which will cost $1.2 billion and employ 300 people, is the largest example so far of cooperation between the private sectors in Egypt and Israel. The Egyptian state is taking a minority stake in the project.
"The project is not made for the sake of politics. It is made because Egypt needs an oil refinery before the year 2000," said Salem, chairman of the private-sector Salem Group.
Salem Group and the Israeli Merhaf Group initiated the project some three years ago and establised MIDOR.
"We found an appropriate business opportunity," he said, "and if we do not do it someone else will do it."
"Moreover, Egypt will consume over 70 percent of the production," he added.
